title: Biting Flies Land on Zebras Less Than a Quarter as Often

scenes.text: In 2019, researchers filmed horseflies around zebras and horses.
The flies circled both at the same rate.
But they landed on zebras less than a quarter as often.
They often bumped into the stripes and flew off again.
Horses in striped coats got fewer landings too.

description:
A 2019 study found horseflies landed on zebras less than a quarter as often as on horses.
The flies often bumped into the stripes and flew off, and horses in striped coats got fewer landings too.
Would you wear a striped coat in fly season?
first_comment: Why do you think zebras have stripes?
